claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi or eutectic multi-principal-element alloys can be used in a homogeneous, coarse-grained, as-cast or conventionally processed initial state.
Laser surface heat treatment near 1000 °C at approximately 4 mm/s can produce an inverse gradient microstructure in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
A subsequent thermal-aging step will stabilize and enhance hierarchical nanotwins.
A subsequent thermal-aging step will promote vermicular eutectic-phase formation.

The proposed laser-plus-aging sequence will generate a single engineered microstructure combining an inverse gradient, partial recrystallization, hierarchical nanotwins, and vermicular eutectic morphology.
The inverse gradient consists of a hard central layer and a soft surface layer.
Retaining partial recrystallization is associated with a favorable strength-ductility combination.
Hierarchical nanotwins contribute to the favorable mechanical response by increasing dislocation-nanotwin interactions.
The soft-surface/hard-core gradient partitions strain and produces hetero-deformation-induced strengthening and hardening.
A kinked vermicular eutectic morphology can improve strength-ductility synergy relative to coarse-grained and conventional straight-morphology EMPEAs.
Vermicular eutectic phases act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Hierarchical nanotwins and vermicular eutectic phases impede crack initiation.
The proposed multi-stage treatment will concurrently enhance yield strength and ductility relative to conventional processing.
The proposed treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20%.
The proposed treatment will improve ductility by 10–15%.
The proposed treatment will enhance Young's modulus.
The proposed treatment will enhance fracture toughness or fracture resistance.
An overly narrow gradient layer increases yield strength at the expense of ductility.
Full recrystallization increases ductility but decreases yield strength.
The method may fail when the selected composition cannot form stable multiphase, hierarchical-twin, or desired eutectic morphologies under the processing conditions.
